_comment: Routing probes. Each is a request with the SHAPE its plan must have.
This exists because 'JARVIS is better now' was previously unfalsifiable. Every
expectation below was verified by hand against the real command before being
written down, so a failure here means behaviour changed, not that the probe was
Judged by FLIPS, not by score. A total that stays at 18/20 while two probes swap
places has hidden a regression behind an average -- so `evaluate` reports P->F and
F->P per probe and treats a single P->F as blocking.
Keep these cheap: routing is deterministic and involves no model, so the whole set
runs in seconds and can gate every commit.

Four probes carry `heldout: true`. `learn` must never read them, and no proposal may be validated against them -- they are the control group. arXiv:2606.28430 (Building to the Test) found that with the oracle in the loop, agents drove scores to near-perfect while shipping code that was 'dead or absent' outside the tested behaviour. GEPA keeps a validation set disjoint from the feedback set for exactly this reason. A gate the optimiser can see is a target, not a gate.

probes.request: fix a typo in the readme
probes.why: the control plane exists to refuse. If this ever convenes a swarm the whole cost argument is dead.
same class of work; must not drift into standard effort

probes.request: add a field to a DocType
probes.why: the core domain case. Must reach the data-model agents.

probes.request: add a field to a form
probes.why: a stranger's wording for the same job. Routed nothing until the triggers were widened.

probes.request: build an approval workflow with a report
probes.why: multi-skill work must batch rather than serialise into one chain

probes.request: add a DocType and test it
probes.why: a validation agent must actually be routed, or the review loop has no panel

probes.request: deploy the retrofit module to production
probes.why: gate 2. The loudest thing the system does; it must not go quiet.

probes.request: drop the audit table and rebuild it
probes.why: gate 1, and it printed nothing at all before the gates were surfaced in plan

humanGates: destructive git operations (force push, history rewrite, branch deletion)

probes.request: deploy to production and drop the audit table
probes.why: naming one gate and swallowing the other is worse than naming neither

probes.request: drop the trailing comma from the list
probes.why: the false-positive case. A gate warning people learn to ignore is worse than none.

probes.request: the production numbers look wrong in the report
probes.why: one signal only -- 'production' as a noun is not a deployment
an unroutable request must degrade to an answer, never to a crash or a full swarm

probes.request: audit the swarm roster for unused agents
probes.why: the system could not route work about itself at all. Six governance agents were unreachable.
asking for a review convened nobody, because code-reviewer's only skill is external

probes.request: review this whitelisted endpoint for injection
probes.why: security-reviewer was added to the roster; an agent nothing can route to is worse than no agent

probes.request: add a whitelisted API for the customer portal
probes.why: the changes that NEED a security review are mostly not described as security work — that is the case nobody thinks to ask about

probes.why: a reviewer convened on everything is one people learn to skip
'permission' alone is far too broad; the unless guard has to hold
